name: The A- and B-Metrics of Ehlers and Kundt
description: The static vacuum fields of algebraic type D beside Schwarzschild's, which Tullio Levi-Civita constructed and Jürgen Ehlers and Wolfgang Kundt named in 1962: the A-metrics have a hyperbolic or a flat plane where Schwarzschild's field has a sphere, and the B-metrics exchange the time with an angle. Two of them, A II and B I, are the field of a tachyon, Schwarzschild's mass boosted past the speed of light, with a cone of unbounded curvature between them.
convention: The constant $b$ is a length. We keep factors of $c$ explicit.
history: Karl Schwarzschild's field of a point mass is the best known of a family, the static vacuum fields whose curvature is of the algebraic type D [schwarzschild1916, hruska2019]. The family is Tullio Levi-Civita's, constructed between 1917 and 1919, and in 1962 Jürgen Ehlers, of Pascual Jordan's seminar at Hamburg, and Wolfgang Kundt set it out in one table and sorted it into classes A, B, and C [bicak2009, ehlerskundt1962]. A I is Schwarzschild's metric [hruska2019]. A II has a hyperbolic plane where Schwarzschild's has a sphere, $r^2(d\chi^2 + \sinh^2\chi\,d\phi^2)$, and $b/r - 1$ where Schwarzschild's has $1 - b/r$, with $b$ a length, and in A III the plane is flat [hruska2019]. Each B-metric is the A-metric of the same number after the exchange $\phi \to it$, $t \to i\phi$, which hands the time to the surface and leaves a length $z$ where the time was [martins1996]. The C-metric is two black holes accelerating in opposite directions, William Kinnersley and Martin Walker's reading of 1970 [bicak2009, kinnersley1970].¶Which sources do the others belong to? One search, M. A. P. Martins's of 1996, put each A- and B-metric into Hermann Weyl's form, where a static vacuum field with an axis has a Newtonian potential, and looked for the masses of that potential, its "Newtonian image sources" [martins1996, weyl1917]. In every case they were half lines of mass, each infinite in one direction [martins1996]. Schwarzschild's field gives a rod of length $b$, B I two half lines with a gap of length $b$ between them, and A III one half line of negative density, which is Abraham Taub's plane symmetric vacuum of 1951 in other coordinates [martins1996, taub1951]. For A II and B II the curvature does not die away far from the lines, and Martins judged the picture "unsatisfactory, or at best incomplete" [martins1996]. B III is Levi-Civita's field of a line of mass at the mass parameter $\sigma = 1/4$, where that field gains a boost symmetry [podolsky2018, wang1997].¶A II had had its source since 1970, and the source was a tachyon, a particle faster than light [hruska2019]. Which gravitational field would such a particle have? Asher Peres's answer was to boost Schwarzschild's mass past the speed of light [peres1970, hruska2019]. A Lorentz boost is allowed only below $c$, but Schwarzschild's metric, in the right coordinates, holds the boosted time $T$, counted as a length, and $Z$ only as squares, and as $v \to \infty$ the squares trade places, $T^2 \to -Z^2$ and $Z^2 \to -T^2$ [hruska2019]. The boosted field is A II inside the cone $T^2 > X^2 + Y^2$, with an imaginary mass, and B I outside it, with a real one [hruska2019]. The mass that sat at the origin for all time now lies along the whole $Z$ axis at the one moment $T = 0$, a particle of infinite speed [hruska2019].¶A jet faster than sound trails a cone of shock, and to L. S. Schulman in 1971 the tachyon's field "is in many ways similar to the shock wave produced by an object moving faster than the signal velocity in a medium" [schulman1971]. For "a dense macroscopic tachyon" he reckoned the wave "capable of exciting Weber's gravitational radiation detection apparatus across astronomical distances" [schulman1971]. The source got its name in 1974 from J. Richard Gott III, the "tachyon singularity", a "spacelike counterpart of the Schwarzschild black hole", and he carried its metric through the horizon with extensions of Martin Kruskal's kind [gott1974, kruskal1960]. The extended metrics show "both normal and time-reversed gravitational Čerenkov cones of high space curvature", and the solutions "correspond to half-advanced, half-retarded fields in accord with the Wheeler-Feynman absorber theory" [gott1974]. The form of the metric suggested to Gott how a tachyon could outrun light with no "transport of energy or information at speeds greater than the velocity of light" [gott1974].¶It took until 2019 for the two halves to be joined: to Ondrej Hruška and Jiří Podolský, A II and B I together are "the complete gravitational field of a tachyon" [hruska2019]. At infinite speed the cone is a cylinder, $X^2 + Y^2 = T^2$, which closes on the $Z$ axis at the speed of light, reaches it at $T = 0$, and opens again [hruska2019]. Slow the tachyon to a finite speed above $c$ and the cylinder becomes a pair of cones with their tips on the particle, the cone behind expanding and the cone ahead contracting [hruska2019]. The particle rides where the two cross, as the crossing point of a pair of scissors can outrun the blades [hruska2019]. The curvature is unbounded on the cone, positive without limit on its inner side and negative without limit on its outer side [hruska2019]. With a cosmological constant the same construction is a tachyon in de Sitter or anti-de Sitter space [hruska2019].¶Inside the cone the time is the interval $\sigma$ from the tachyon's line, and $\sigma = b$ is a horizon [hruska2019]. For $\sigma > b$ the field changes with $\sigma$, and for $\sigma < b$ it is static, with $\sigma$ a radius measured from a singularity that is timelike [hruska2019]. Outside the cone the radius $r$ never falls below $b$ [hruska2019]. Ehlers and Kundt's continuation through $r = b$, of 1962, joins two asymptotically flat regions through a neck, where $\tau$ and $\phi$ span a de Sitter space of two dimensions and radius $b$ [ehlerskundt1962, hruska2019]. B II has no flat limit as $b \to 0$, and its physical meaning, Podolský, Hruška, and Jerry Griffiths concluded in 2018, is "unclear" [podolsky2018].

related.text: A I, the first of the family. B I is Schwarzschild's metric with the time and the angle exchanged [martins1996], and A II and B I together are Schwarzschild's field boosted past the speed of light [hruska2019].
At $b = 0$ A II and B I are flat, the inside and the outside of the cone $T^2 = X^2 + Y^2$ in Minkowski space. A III, B II, and B III have no flat member.
Class C of Ehlers and Kundt's table, the static vacuum fields of type D that admit no isotropy group [ehlerskundt1962, bicak2009].

Levi-Civita's field of a line of mass holds two of the family. B III is the cylinder at $\sigma = 1/4$ [podolsky2018], and A III, Taub's plane symmetric vacuum, is the cylinder at $\sigma = -1/2$ [martins1996, wang1997].
A II and A III with a negative cosmological constant added, the black holes with hyperbolic and flat horizons [hruska2019]. As $L \to \infty$ the hyperbolic hole with $\mu = -b$ is A II.
A III with $b$ made negative, so that its radius is a time, is Kasner's universe with exponents $(-\tfrac{1}{3}, \tfrac{2}{3}, \tfrac{2}{3})$.
Schwarzschild's mass boosted to the speed of light exactly. As the tachyon slows to $c$ its two cones close into one plane of shock moving with it [hruska2019].
The continued B I joins two asymptotically flat regions through a neck at $r = b$, as Einstein and Rosen's bridge joins two through Schwarzschild's horizon [hruska2019].

Schwarzschild's A I with the NUT parameter $l$ added. The B-metrics take a parameter of the same kind, which removes their singularity as $l$ removes Schwarzschild's, and Jerzy Plebański called that family the anti-NUT solution [podolsky2018].

coordinates.name: A II, Static

parameters.description: Ehlers and Kundt's constant, a length; in the A I metric it is the Schwarzschild radius $2GM/c^2$ of a mass $M$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \chi, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The surfaces of constant $t$ and $r$ are hyperbolic planes of curvature $-1/r^2$.

coordinates.name: A II, Inside the Cone

parameters.description: Ehlers and Kundt's constant, a length; in the A I metric it is the Schwarzschild radius $2GM/c^2$ of a mass $M$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(\sigma, z, \chi, \phi)$, where the time $\sigma$ is a length and continues the static chart's $r$ beyond the horizon $r = b$, and $z$ continues its $ct$.

coordinates.name: A II, Kruskal

parameters.description: Ehlers and Kundt's constant, a length; in the A I metric it is the Schwarzschild radius $2GM/c^2$ of a mass $M$

Radius of the hyperbolic planes, a length, the solution of $\left(r/b - 1\right)e^{r/b} = UV$, with $\mathrm{W}$ the principal branch of Lambert's function, $\mathrm{W}(x)\,e^{\mathrm{W}(x)} = x$; its derivatives are $\partial_U r = b^2\,V e^{-r/b}/r$ and $\partial_V r = b^2\,U e^{-r/b}/r$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(U, V, \chi, \phi)$, with $U$ and $V$ null and dimensionless. Where $r < b$ they are $U = -\sqrt{1 - r/b}\,e^{(r - ct)/2b}$ and $V = \sqrt{1 - r/b}\,e^{(r + ct)/2b}$ in the static chart's $t$ and $r$, and the radius $r$ is a function of $UV$.

coordinates.name: A II, Inertial

parameters.description: Ehlers and Kundt's constant, a length; in the A I metric it is the Schwarzschild radius $2GM/c^2$ of a mass $M$
Interval from the line $T = X = Y = 0$, a length, the time $\sigma$ of the chart inside the cone

coordinates.convention: We use the inertial coordinates $(T, X, Y, Z)$ of the flat spacetime at $b = 0$, all lengths, with $T$ the time multiplied by $c$. They are $T = \sigma\cosh\chi$, $X = \sigma\sinh\chi\cos\phi$, $Y = \sigma\sinh\chi\sin\phi$, and $Z = z$ in the coordinates $(\sigma, z, \chi, \phi)$ beyond the horizon.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = -dT^2 + dX^2 + dY^2 + dZ^2 - \dfrac{b}{\sigma}\left(dZ^2 + \dfrac{\left(T\,dT - X\,dX - Y\,dY\right)^2}{\sigma\left(\sigma - b\right)}\right)
geodesics: \ddot{T} - \dfrac{b\,T\left(\sigma^3 + 3\sigma\,X^2 + 3\sigma\,Y^2 - 2b\,X^2 - 2b\,Y^2\right)}{2\sigma^5\left(\sigma - b\right)}\dot{T}^2 + \dfrac{b\,X\left(3\sigma - 2b\right)\left(\sigma^2 + X^2 + Y^2\right)}{\sigma^5\left(\sigma - b\right)}\dot{T}\dot{X} + \dfrac{b\,Y\left(3\sigma - 2b\right)\left(\sigma^2 + X^2 + Y^2\right)}{\sigma^5\left(\sigma - b\right)}\dot{T}\dot{Y} - \dfrac{b\,T\left(2\sigma^3 + 3\sigma\,X^2 - 2\sigma^2\,b - 2b\,X^2\right)}{2\sigma^5\left(\sigma - b\right)}\dot{X}^2 - \dfrac{b\,T\,X\,Y\left(3\sigma - 2b\right)}{\sigma^5\left(\sigma - b\right)}\dot{X}\dot{Y} - \dfrac{b\,T\left(2\sigma^3 + 3\sigma\,Y^2 - 2\sigma^2\,b - 2b\,Y^2\right)}{2\sigma^5\left(\sigma - b\right)}\dot{Y}^2 + \dfrac{b\,T\left(\sigma - b\right)}{2\sigma^4}\dot{Z}^2 = 0

\ddot{X} - \dfrac{b\,X\left(\sigma^3 + 3\sigma\,X^2 + 3\sigma\,Y^2 - 2b\,X^2 - 2b\,Y^2\right)}{2\sigma^5\left(\sigma - b\right)}\dot{T}^2 + \dfrac{b\,T\,X^2\left(3\sigma - 2b\right)}{\sigma^5\left(\sigma - b\right)}\dot{T}\dot{X} + \dfrac{b\,T\,X\,Y\left(3\sigma - 2b\right)}{\sigma^5\left(\sigma - b\right)}\dot{T}\dot{Y} - \dfrac{b\,X\left(2\sigma^3 + 3\sigma\,X^2 - 2\sigma^2\,b - 2b\,X^2\right)}{2\sigma^5\left(\sigma - b\right)}\dot{X}^2 - \dfrac{b\,X^2\,Y\left(3\sigma - 2b\right)}{\sigma^5\left(\sigma - b\right)}\dot{X}\dot{Y} - \dfrac{b\,X\left(2\sigma^3 + 3\sigma\,Y^2 - 2\sigma^2\,b - 2b\,Y^2\right)}{2\sigma^5\left(\sigma - b\right)}\dot{Y}^2 + \dfrac{b\,X\left(\sigma - b\right)}{2\sigma^4}\dot{Z}^2 = 0

\ddot{Y} - \dfrac{b\,Y\left(\sigma^3 + 3\sigma\,X^2 + 3\sigma\,Y^2 - 2b\,X^2 - 2b\,Y^2\right)}{2\sigma^5\left(\sigma - b\right)}\dot{T}^2 + \dfrac{b\,T\,X\,Y\left(3\sigma - 2b\right)}{\sigma^5\left(\sigma - b\right)}\dot{T}\dot{X} + \dfrac{b\,T\,Y^2\left(3\sigma - 2b\right)}{\sigma^5\left(\sigma - b\right)}\dot{T}\dot{Y} - \dfrac{b\,Y\left(2\sigma^3 + 3\sigma\,X^2 - 2\sigma^2\,b - 2b\,X^2\right)}{2\sigma^5\left(\sigma - b\right)}\dot{X}^2 - \dfrac{b\,X\,Y^2\left(3\sigma - 2b\right)}{\sigma^5\left(\sigma - b\right)}\dot{X}\dot{Y} - \dfrac{b\,Y\left(2\sigma^3 + 3\sigma\,Y^2 - 2\sigma^2\,b - 2b\,Y^2\right)}{2\sigma^5\left(\sigma - b\right)}\dot{Y}^2 + \dfrac{b\,Y\left(\sigma - b\right)}{2\sigma^4}\dot{Z}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: B I, Static

parameters.description: Ehlers and Kundt's constant, a length; in the A I metric it is the Schwarzschild radius $2GM/c^2$ of a mass $M$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(\tau, r, \theta, z)$, with the time $\tau$ dimensionless and $z$ a length.

coordinates.name: B I, Outside the Cone

parameters.description: Ehlers and Kundt's constant, a length; in the A I metric it is the Schwarzschild radius $2GM/c^2$ of a mass $M$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(\tau, r, \phi, z)$, with the time $\tau$ dimensionless and $z$ a length. The surfaces of constant $r$ and $z$ are de Sitter spaces of two dimensions and radius $r$.

coordinates.name: B I, Through the Neck

parameters.description: Ehlers and Kundt's constant, a length; in the A I metric it is the Schwarzschild radius $2GM/c^2$ of a mass $M$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(\tau, \rho, \phi, z)$, with $\tau$ and $\rho$ dimensionless and $z$ a length. The radius is $r = b/(1 - \rho^2)$, so each sign of $\rho$ covers $r > b$ once.

coordinates.name: B I, Inertial
domains: X^2 + Y^2 > T^2 + b^2 \;\text{(outside the cone, } r > b\text{)}

parameters.description: Ehlers and Kundt's constant, a length; in the A I metric it is the Schwarzschild radius $2GM/c^2$ of a mass $M$
Interval from the line $T = X = Y = 0$, a length, the radius $r$ of the chart outside the cone

coordinates.convention: We use the inertial coordinates $(T, X, Y, Z)$ of the flat spacetime at $b = 0$, all lengths, with $T$ the time multiplied by $c$. They are $T = r\sinh\tau$, $X = r\cosh\tau\cos\phi$, $Y = r\cosh\tau\sin\phi$, and $Z = z$ in the coordinates $(\tau, r, \phi, z)$ of the de Sitter slicing.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = -dT^2 + dX^2 + dY^2 + dZ^2 - \dfrac{b}{r}\left(dZ^2 - \dfrac{\left(T\,dT - X\,dX - Y\,dY\right)^2}{r\left(r - b\right)}\right)
geodesics: \ddot{T} + \dfrac{b\,T\left(r^3 - 3r\,X^2 - 3r\,Y^2 + 2b\,X^2 + 2b\,Y^2\right)}{2r^5\left(r - b\right)}\dot{T}^2 - \dfrac{b\,X\left(3r - 2b\right)\left(r^2 - X^2 - Y^2\right)}{r^5\left(r - b\right)}\dot{T}\dot{X} - \dfrac{b\,Y\left(3r - 2b\right)\left(r^2 - X^2 - Y^2\right)}{r^5\left(r - b\right)}\dot{T}\dot{Y} + \dfrac{b\,T\left(2r^3 - 3r\,X^2 - 2r^2\,b + 2b\,X^2\right)}{2r^5\left(r - b\right)}\dot{X}^2 - \dfrac{b\,T\,X\,Y\left(3r - 2b\right)}{r^5\left(r - b\right)}\dot{X}\dot{Y} + \dfrac{b\,T\left(2r^3 - 3r\,Y^2 - 2r^2\,b + 2b\,Y^2\right)}{2r^5\left(r - b\right)}\dot{Y}^2 - \dfrac{b\,T\left(r - b\right)}{2r^4}\dot{Z}^2 = 0

\ddot{X} + \dfrac{b\,X\left(r^3 - 3r\,X^2 - 3r\,Y^2 + 2b\,X^2 + 2b\,Y^2\right)}{2r^5\left(r - b\right)}\dot{T}^2 + \dfrac{b\,T\,X^2\left(3r - 2b\right)}{r^5\left(r - b\right)}\dot{T}\dot{X} + \dfrac{b\,T\,X\,Y\left(3r - 2b\right)}{r^5\left(r - b\right)}\dot{T}\dot{Y} + \dfrac{b\,X\left(2r^3 - 3r\,X^2 - 2r^2\,b + 2b\,X^2\right)}{2r^5\left(r - b\right)}\dot{X}^2 - \dfrac{b\,X^2\,Y\left(3r - 2b\right)}{r^5\left(r - b\right)}\dot{X}\dot{Y} + \dfrac{b\,X\left(2r^3 - 3r\,Y^2 - 2r^2\,b + 2b\,Y^2\right)}{2r^5\left(r - b\right)}\dot{Y}^2 - \dfrac{b\,X\left(r - b\right)}{2r^4}\dot{Z}^2 = 0

\ddot{Y} + \dfrac{b\,Y\left(r^3 - 3r\,X^2 - 3r\,Y^2 + 2b\,X^2 + 2b\,Y^2\right)}{2r^5\left(r - b\right)}\dot{T}^2 + \dfrac{b\,T\,X\,Y\left(3r - 2b\right)}{r^5\left(r - b\right)}\dot{T}\dot{X} + \dfrac{b\,T\,Y^2\left(3r - 2b\right)}{r^5\left(r - b\right)}\dot{T}\dot{Y} + \dfrac{b\,Y\left(2r^3 - 3r\,X^2 - 2r^2\,b + 2b\,X^2\right)}{2r^5\left(r - b\right)}\dot{X}^2 - \dfrac{b\,X\,Y^2\left(3r - 2b\right)}{r^5\left(r - b\right)}\dot{X}\dot{Y} + \dfrac{b\,Y\left(2r^3 - 3r\,Y^2 - 2r^2\,b + 2b\,Y^2\right)}{2r^5\left(r - b\right)}\dot{Y}^2 - \dfrac{b\,Y\left(r - b\right)}{2r^4}\dot{Z}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: A III

parameters.description: Ehlers and Kundt's constant, a length; in the A I metric it is the Schwarzschild radius $2GM/c^2$ of a mass $M$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \chi, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\chi$ dimensionless, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The surfaces of constant $t$ and $r$ are flat planes with polar coordinates $r\chi$ and $\phi$.

coordinates.name: B II, Static

parameters.description: Ehlers and Kundt's constant, a length; in the A I metric it is the Schwarzschild radius $2GM/c^2$ of a mass $M$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(\tau, r, \chi, z)$, with the time $\tau$ dimensionless and $z$ a length. The surfaces of constant $r$ and $z$ are anti-de Sitter spaces of two dimensions and radius $r$.

coordinates.name: B II, Through the Axis

parameters.description: Ehlers and Kundt's constant, a length; in the A I metric it is the Schwarzschild radius $2GM/c^2$ of a mass $M$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(\tau, \rho, \chi, z)$, with $\tau$, $\rho$, and $\chi$ dimensionless and $z$ a length. The radius is $r = b/(1 + \rho^2)$, and $\tau$ and $\chi$ are the static coordinates of anti-de Sitter space of two dimensions.

coordinates.name: B III

parameters.description: Ehlers and Kundt's constant, a length; in the A I metric it is the Schwarzschild radius $2GM/c^2$ of a mass $M$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(\tau, r, x, z)$, with $\tau$ and $x$ dimensionless and $z$ a length.
